{"summary":"Replace both distinct failure paths with one generic result, preferably `{ ok: false, error: \"invalid credentials\" }`, while leaving the success result unchanged. This is the smallest change that removes username disclosure from the function’s return value; timing resistance would require a broader password-verification redesign.","claims":[{"id":"C1","statement":"The current return value explicitly distinguishes an absent username from an incorrect password.","kind":"fact","confidence":"high","evidence":["src/login.js:5 returns error \"unknown user\" when the lookup fails.","src/login.js:6 returns error \"wrong password\" when the password check fails."],"followup_status":null},{"id":"C2","statement":"Those distinct errors allow a caller to enumerate registered usernames without knowing their passwords.","kind":"inference","confidence":"high","evidence":["src/login.js:4-6 branches on whether `users.get(username)` returned a user and exposes that branch through different error strings."],"followup_status":null},{"id":"C3","statement":"The smallest safe response-level change is to make both failure cases return the same generic object, which can be expressed as `if (!user || user.password !== password) return { ok: false, error: \"invalid credentials\" };`.","kind":"inference","confidence":"high","evidence":["src/login.js:4-7 contains only the lookup, two failure returns, and the successful userId return."],"followup_status":null},{"id":"C4","statement":"No project call sites or tests depend on either existing error string.","kind":"fact","confidence":"high","evidence":["`rg -n \"login|unknown user|wrong password|invalid credentials\" .` found only src/login.js and a README description; no invocation was found."],"followup_status":null},{"id":"C5","statement":"Combining the branch removes the explicit response leak but does not provide strong timing-enumeration resistance because password comparison is skipped when the username is absent.","kind":"inference","confidence":"high","evidence":["src/login.js:4-6 performs no password comparison after a failed user lookup.","The proposed `||` expression also short-circuits when `user` is absent."],"followup_status":null},{"id":"C6","statement":"If timing enumeration is in scope, absent usernames should undergo the same password-hash verification operation against a fixed dummy hash as existing usernames.","kind":"inference","confidence":"high","evidence":["src/login.js:4-6 currently performs different work depending on whether the username exists."],"followup_status":null}],"open_questions":["Does the threat model require resistance to remote timing-based username enumeration, or only removal of the explicit error-message oracle? If timing is in scope, the generic-return patch alone is insufficient."]}
